title: David Bowie
scene: British music hall / Swinging London theatrical pop
notes: Edwardian character sketches and elaborate music-hall pop before the signature Bowie sound.

title: David Bowie (1969)
scene: Late-1960s British psychedelic folk and art rock
notes: Folk-psychedelic narratives and ambitious arrangements; originally issued under Bowie’s own name.

title: The Man Who Sold the World
scene: Early British hard rock and pre-glam experimentation
notes: Ronson’s heavy riffs and Visconti’s prominent bass frame paranoid, surreal songs.

title: Hunky Dory
scene: British art rock and emergent glam rock
sounds_like: Lou Reed|The Velvet Underground|Elton John|George Harrison|T. Rex
notes: Piano-led art rock, elaborate strings, intimate storytelling and an early glam-rock spark.

title: The Rise and Fall of Ziggy Stardust and the Spiders from Mars
influenced_by: T. Rex|The Velvet Underground|Iggy Pop|Lou Reed|Vince Taylor
notes: Apocalyptic glam-rock storytelling pairs Ronson riffs with ambitious theatrical arrangements.

title: Aladdin Sane
scene: British glam rock and US-tour rock
notes: Glam rock collides with Garson’s dissonant piano and American street imagery.

title: Pin Ups
scene: British glam rock covers of 1964–67 London club repertoire
sounds_like: The Who|The Yardbirds|The Pretty Things|The Kinks
influenced_by: The Pretty Things|Them|The Yardbirds|Pink Floyd|The Mojos|The Who|The Easybeats|The Merseys|The Kinks
notes: A guitar-driven tribute to the British club music that shaped Bowie.

title: Diamond Dogs
scene: Late British glam rock; dystopian theatrical rock with emerging soul
sounds_like: The Rolling Stones|Roxy Music|Iggy Pop|Barry White
notes: Dystopian theatrical rock blends fractured glam guitars with emerging soul and funk.

title: Young Americans
scene: Philadelphia soul / mid-1970s American R&B crossover
sounds_like: The O’Jays|Harold Melvin & the Blue Notes|Hall & Oates|Curtis Mayfield
notes: Philadelphia soul experiment built around live rhythm players, intricate harmonies and uneasy fame.

title: Station to Station
scene: Los Angeles plastic soul meets European experimental rock
sounds_like: Kraftwerk|Neu!|Roxy Music|Iggy Pop|Sly and the Family Stone
notes: Austere electronic ambitions collide with sensual funk rhythms and the Thin White Duke.

title: Low
scene: French-recorded / Berlin-mixed experimental electronic art rock
notes: Fragmented rhythm songs yield to disquieting ambient instrumentals, with radically treated drums.

title: “Heroes”
scene: West Berlin Hansa experimental art rock / Berlin trilogy
notes: Fripp’s feedback and spacious Berlin recordings intensify restless rock and atmospheric instrumentals.

title: Lodger
scene: Late-1970s art rock / experimental new wave; Berlin trilogy
notes: Angular guitars, rhythmic experiments and travel narratives replace ambient suites with compact songs.

title: Scary Monsters (And Super Creeps)
scene: British post-punk and art rock / early-1980s new wave
notes: Fripp’s jagged guitars and electronic treatments frame anxious, compact art-rock songs.

title: Let's Dance
scene: Early-1980s transatlantic post-disco dance rock and blue-eyed soul
notes: Rodgers blends Chic-like grooves, horns and blues guitar into polished crossover dance-rock.

title: Tonight
scene: Mid-1980s polished pop-rock, reggae-inflected crossover and sophisti-pop
notes: Glossy horn-rich pop mixes new material, Iggy Pop remakes and reggae-styled covers.

title: Blackstar
scene: New York jazz musicians / late-career British art rock
notes: Noir jazz combo, skittering beats and synths around songs of mortality; his farewell.
